data.title: AI Tutoring with Khanmigo in a Two-Year School Experiment
data.author: bryan0
data.article_summary: 文章介绍一项为期两年的随机实验：田纳西州18所中学学生在补救数学课中使用Khan Academy及AI导师Khanmigo。使用AI使数学成绩每学期提高约1.3个全国百分位，效果与普通平台练习相近。尽管96%的学生至少尝试过Khanmigo，但使用频率低、数学对话浅薄。研究指出，AI辅导的关键限制不是获取途径，而是学生的实际参与度。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI辅导工具对补救性学生的实际效果有限，核心瓶颈可能不是工具能力，而是学生的参与度与持续使用。

不同观点：
• **强化督促型**：ilaksh认为补救学生往往缺乏主动性，AI应更积极介入，例如设置 inactivity 计时器，并对不完成任务设置现实后果；同时应在平均或优等生群体中进一步研究。  
• **参与度优先型**：parsimo2010、firejake308认为研究显示提升很小，关键在于学生是否真正使用工具；再好的AI也无法自动激发学习兴趣。  
• **教师主导型**：bakul认为“先让学生参与，再谈AI辅导”的逻辑可能本末倒置，优秀教师才是激发兴趣的核心，AI最多辅助教师提升教学。  
• **个体差异型**：zhivota指出孩子对AI tutor的接受度不同，有人能借助AI快速学习，有人仍需传统的、能培养参与感的教学。  
• **效果比较型**：nerevarthelame认为，AI辅导的学习效果大致相当于无AI自学，约为真人辅导的四分之一；但若AI能促使部分学生投入学习，仍具有成本优势。

补充讨论：争议焦点是应优先改进AI并强制学生使用，还是先解决教学中的参与和兴趣问题。另有评论质疑论文摘要由AI生成，提醒关注研究质量与可信度。

One Click Away: AI Tutoring with Khanmigo in a Two-Year School Experiment
Philip Oreopoulos
,
Nina Low
August 2026
Generative AI has been promoted as the technology that could transform education by providing every student a personal tutor. We provide some of the first large-scale experimental evidence, from a two-year cluster randomized trial in 18 Tennessee middle schools in which randomly assigned students used Khan Academy with its AI tutor, Khanmigo, configured to coach rather than give answers, during existing daily remedial mathematics sessions. Assignment raises math achievement by 1.3 national percentile ranks per term, or about 0.06 to 0.08 standard deviations over a school year; the implied effect of a full year of active participation reaches 0.14 standard deviations. These gains resemble those from Khan Academy practice without AI assistance. One explanation is that students used the tutor infrequently and, when they did, rarely engaged it in substantive mathematical dialogue: 96 percent of students tried Khanmigo at least once, but the median student messaged it on only a third of the days they practiced, and in only 17 percent of the exercise sessions in which they made a mistake. Messages that students did send were mostly bare answers or clicks on suggested prompts. The binding constraint appears to be engagement: realizing the promise of AI tutoring will require getting students to use it, not just giving them access.

Artificial intelligence; AI tutoring; Khanmigo; computer-assisted learning; educational technology; field experiment; math achievement; student engagement; response to intervention

data.title: Dust: Pretraining Transformers Without Backpropagation
data.author: E-Reverance
data.article_summary: 文章提出Dust：一种通过逐token扰动激活、依据损失变化加权平均来估计梯度的零阶优化方法，旨在替代反向传播训练Transformer语言模型。Dust利用“虚拟种群”并行评估，效率远高于权重空间进化策略；随着种群和模型规模扩大，其梯度与反向传播更一致，部分实验甚至超越后者，显示零阶方法在计算充足时具备扩展潜力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 Dust 等零阶/无梯度优化方法能否替代或补充反向传播，以及其效率、适用场景和发展潜力展开讨论。

不同观点：
• **反对替代反向传播**：blt认为神经网络目标通常平滑或Lipschitz，梯度能直接指示改进方向，参数越多优势越明显；零阶方法在复杂度上存在理论劣势，更值得发展的是利用网络结构的梯度优化器，如Muon。  
• **对Dust优势持怀疑态度**：syntacticsalt指出Dust及一阶方法都可能平滑损失，论文未充分讨论凸性；即使零阶方法扩展性更好，也未必能形成超过改进型一阶方法的优势，除非面对无法提供梯度的模拟器等环境。  
• **支持作为特殊场景工具**：mkaic认为零阶优化不是“反向传播替代品”，但适合反向传播困难的情形，如不进行BPTT训练大型RNN、训练可微但难优化的神经计算机。  
• **认可更广泛的探索能力**：usernametaken29认为进化方法更通用，可能绕开Hessian条件数限制，但代价高、近似暴力搜索；polyomino建议先用反向传播训练，再用Dust微调。  
• **关注工程与硬件价值**：部分评论认为其优势可能在并行化、无全局时钟的信用分配、光学或内存内计算等新硬件场景，而非传统训练效率。

补充讨论：争议核心是“零阶方法是否能在实际成本、能耗、内存和下游质量上超越反向传播”。评论者要求在相同损失下比较墙钟时间、能源和峰值内存，并质疑其高计算成本及大模型所需采样规模。

49970871.article_content:
TL;DR
We present the first zeroth-order method that is competitive with backprop at pretraining transformer language models. Dust perturbs activations (node perturbation) independently at every token, so each token is a
virtual
population member and one forward pass evaluates them all in parallel.
Dust approximates backprop closely at large population (i.e. substantially more compute) and in multiple settings even
exceeds
it. This hints that in a compute-rich regime we might be able to surpass backprop.
Dust is orders of magnitude more efficient than weight-space ES. From 1M tokens up, Dust is on the order of $10^3$ to $10^4$ times more efficient than a transformer implementation of EGGROLL, a state-of-the-art ES method, based on our extrapolations.
Zeroth-order methods are widely believed not to scale to large networks. Strikingly, we find larger models are more population-efficient, not less: a 243M-parameter model outperforms a $120\times$ smaller model at most population sizes.
Dust’s gradient estimates align better with backprop’s as population grows, and stay well aligned at every scale we test, up to 1B tokens, which is encouraging for scaling.
1
Introduction
Deep learning has been built around backprop, the only credit assignment algorithm capable of training modern neural nets, including transformer-based language models. Backprop requires differentiability and produces first-order gradients, and deep learning’s architectures, optimizers, and hardware have co-evolved around this constraint.
However, as the amount of compute available in the world increases, we might prefer more generic and brute-force learning algorithms based on
search
over inductive biases like differentiability, backprop, and approximations of higher-order gradients. The bitter lesson
(
Sutton, 2019
Richard S. Sutton. The bitter lesson.
http://www.incompleteideas.net/IncIdeas/BitterLesson.html
, 2019. Blog post.
)
is that general methods that scale with compute eventually win, and AlphaGo Zero
(
Silver et al., 2017
David Silver, Julian Schrittwieser, Karen Simonyan, Ioannis Antonoglou, Aja Huang, Arthur Guez, Thomas Hubert, Lucas Baker, Matthew Lai, Adrian Bolton, Yutian Chen, Timothy Lillicrap, Fan Hui, Laurent Sifre, George van den Driessche, Thore Graepel, and Demis Hassabis. Mastering the game of Go without human knowledge.
Nature
, 550 (7676): 354–359, 2017. doi:
10.1038/nature24270
.
)
is the obvious example. Bootstrapping AlphaGo on human data helped the network learn faster initially, but with a lot of computation the purely self-play network overtook it. Similarly, differentiability and backprop might be good inductive biases in the low-compute regime, where they make learning efficient, but in the high-compute regime they limit the space of architectures that work. Even within an architecture, gradient-based methods fail to explore the loss landscape optimally
(
Liu et al., 2020
Shengchao Liu, Dimitris Papailiopoulos, and Dimitris Achlioptas. Bad global minima exist and SGD can reach them. In
Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
, volume 33, 2020.
)
. This might also explain why current neural nets require massive amounts of data to generalize. A more flexible credit assignment algorithm based on search is likely an important step towards much better generalization.
In this paper, we aim to replace backprop with a learning algorithm based much more on brute-force computation and much less on analytic structure. We call it Dust. Dust is a zeroth-order optimization algorithm that perturbs activations, rewards each perturbation by how much it lowers the loss, and averages the reward-weighted perturbations over a population to estimate the gradient. Traditional ES methods that perturb weights
(
Salimans et al., 2017
Tim Salimans, Jonathan Ho, Xi Chen, Szymon Sidor, and Ilya Sutskever. Evolution strategies as a scalable alternative to reinforcement learning.
arXiv preprint arXiv:1703.03864
, 2017.
)
, like EGGROLL
(
Sarkar et al., 2025
Bidipta Sarkar, Mattie Fellows, Juan Agustin Duque, Alistair Letcher, Antonio León Villares, Anya Sims, Clarisse Wibault, Dmitry Samsonov, Dylan Cope, Jarek Liesen, Kang Li, Lukas Seier, Theo Wolf, Uljad Berdica, Valentin Mohl, Alexander David Goldie, Aaron Courville, Karin Sevegnani, Shimon Whiteson, and Jakob Nicolaus Foerster. Evolution strategies at the hyperscale.
arXiv preprint arXiv:2511.16652
, 2025.
)
, scale with population, but scaling the population is costly because each member must be materialized and evaluated. We remove both costs with the concept of
virtual population
, where we avoid materializing every member by bypassing weight space entirely and instead perturb activations, as in node perturbation
(
Werfel et al., 2003
Justin Werfel, Xiaohui Xie, and H. Sebastian Seung. Learning curves for stochastic gradient descent in linear feedforward networks. In
Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
, volume 16, 2003.
;
Widrow and Lehr, 1990
Bernard Widrow a

data.title: ChatGPT is adding real cartoonists' signatures to fake New Yorker cartoons
data.author: rdmuser
data.article_summary: 文章报道，ChatGPT生成“《纽约客》风格”漫画时，不仅模仿杂志画风，还擅自复制并添加真实漫画家的签名，导致作品被误认为出自本人。布伦丹·洛珀等15名以上漫画家称此举侵犯身份与署名权。OpenAI承认是模型漏洞并加强限制，但问题仍未完全解决。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：生成式AI在模仿特定艺术风格时，会把艺术家的签名或印章错误地当作风格元素生成，引发抄袭、误导和法律责任争议。

不同观点：
• **批评与追责派**：认为这本质上是“Plagiarism as a Service”或“版权洗白机器”。如果个人伪造艺术家签名可能被起诉，LLM厂商也应承担相应责任；商业订阅模式还可能支持“姓名/形象权”等诉讼。  
• **技术解释派**：模型并不理解签名的身份和法律含义，只是从训练数据中学到“某种画风—签名位于角落”的统计关联，因此会产生视觉拼接错误。这并非OpenAI独有，早期Stable Diffusion生成浮世绘时也常自动添加不相关的“印章”。  
• **责任归因派**：有人认为用户在公开发布前应检查并删除假签名；但也有人指出，普通用户经常注意不到，例如公司演示中管理者直接使用了带有“bloper”假签名的漫画。  
• **能力质疑派**：该现象被用来反驳“LLM能够推理”以及“AI只是像人一样犯错”的说法，认为这种错误体现了模型缺乏基本语境理解。  
• **改进派**：主张厂商应像限制输出书籍原文那样，专门训练模型避免生成真实艺术家的签名。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于这是可通过工程修正的模型缺陷，还是反映了生成式AI商业模式对创作者作品的系统性挪用；同时涉及厂商、用户及法律制度各自应承担多大责任。

ChatGPT is adding real cartoonists’ signatures to fake New Yorker cartoons
OpenAI’s chatbot isn’t just imitating the magazine’s style. It’s also falsely attributing AI-generated images to real artists.
Nieman Lab commissioned
Brendan Loper
to draw a cartoon reflecting on his experience with ChatGPT reproducing his signature.
By
Andrew Deck
Oct.  5, 2026, 4:01 p.m.
At the pearly gates, Dolly Parton, in a sparkling gown, stands arm in arm with Tim Curry, dressed as Dr. Frank-N-Furter. “I knew I chose the right plus one,” Parton says to God, who is standing at heaven’s reception desk.
That’s the premise of
a cartoon that went viral on Twitter
in the days after the legendary entertainers’ deaths in late August. One tweet of the cartoon received 25,000 likes, while other versions of the image circulated on
Facebook
,
Instagram
, and
Bluesky
.
In the bottom right corner of the cartoon is the pen name “BLOPER,” the signature of New Yorker cartoonist
Brendan Loper
. But Loper didn’t draw the cartoon, or sign it. It was generated by ChatGPT and
first posted
to Facebook by a Dolly Parton fan. In the comments section of her post, she wrote she had simply asked ChatGPT to make “a New Yorker-style cartoon.”
“I had people writing to me about this cartoon, asking if it was mine,” Loper told me. First came a text from his twin brother, whose friend had seen the AI-generated image. Emails and DMs on social media from strangers followed. “It was very surreal,” he said.
A cartoon generated by ChatGPT and signed with Brendan Loper’s signature that was
posted to Twitter on August 26, 2026
.
This wasn’t the first time ChatGPT had reproduced Loper’s signature. In May, a stranger reached out over Instagram to warn Loper that his pen name had appeared in an image output by the chatbot. Over the summer, Loper found additional examples in a
Reddit forum
about ChatGPT, where users had been posting similar New Yorker-style cartoons they had generated.
Loper already knew his work was “out there, getting harvested for all of this [AI] training,” he said. But an image generator faking his signature felt more personal. “I’m not a territorial person, but my name is my name. It felt very much like a violation of my personhood.”
RELATED ARTICLE
“I don’t want to outsource my brain”: How political cartoonists are bringing AI into their work
Andrew Deck
June 2, 2025
These days, cartoon signatures are more than a byline. In an era where cartoons are regularly stripped from their original context and circulated on blogs and social media without proper licensing, they can also act as a watermark that ties an illustration to its original creator.
“The signature for me is the certificate of authenticity. I only put it on work that I’m putting on the internet that I feel needs to be recognized as from my hand,” Loper told me. “If I put my name on it, it’s official, it’s mine. It really is a brand. It’s the mark that I made.”
Loper isn’t the only New Yorker cartoonist whose signature has been reproduced by ChatGPT. In the same online forums are dozens of images with those of other prominent contributors, including
Harry Bliss
,
Emily Flake
,
Joe Dator
,
Pat Byrnes
,
Peter Vey
, and
Jason Adam Katzenstein
. In my own tests, ChatGPT output cartoons with signatures of some of the magazine’s most established cartoonists, past and present, including
George Booth
,
Liza Donnelly
,
Ellis Rosen
, and
Saul Steinberg
. In all, I documented more than 15 New Yorker cartoonists whose signatures have been used by OpenAI’s image generator without permission or compensation.
“We believe the future of creativity is one that is fundamentally human, and our focus is on building tools that empower human creativity and creators,” said a spokesperson for OpenAI in a statement. “We very much appreciate the community flagging bugs and unintended behavior by our models, so we can address them.”

49971846.article_summary: 文章报道，ChatGPT生成“《纽约客》风格”漫画时，不仅模仿杂志画风，还擅自复制并添加真实漫画家的签名，导致作品被误认为出自本人。布伦丹·洛珀等15名以上漫画家称此举侵犯身份与署名权。OpenAI承认是模型漏洞并加强限制，但问题仍未完全解决。
49971846.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：生成式AI在模仿特定艺术风格时，会把艺术家的签名或印章错误地当作风格元素生成，引发抄袭、误导和法律责任争议。

不同观点：
• **批评与追责派**：认为这本质上是“Plagiarism as a Service”或“版权洗白机器”。如果个人伪造艺术家签名可能被起诉，LLM厂商也应承担相应责任；商业订阅模式还可能支持“姓名/形象权”等诉讼。  
• **技术解释派**：模型并不理解签名的身份和法律含义，只是从训练数据中学到“某种画风—签名位于角落”的统计关联，因此会产生视觉拼接错误。这并非OpenAI独有，早期Stable Diffusion生成浮世绘时也常自动添加不相关的“印章”。  
• **责任归因派**：有人认为用户在公开发布前应检查并删除假签名；但也有人指出，普通用户经常注意不到，例如公司演示中管理者直接使用了带有“bloper”假签名的漫画。  
• **能力质疑派**：该现象被用来反驳“LLM能够推理”以及“AI只是像人一样犯错”的说法，认为这种错误体现了模型缺乏基本语境理解。  
• **改进派**：主张厂商应像限制输出书籍原文那样，专门训练模型避免生成真实艺术家的签名。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于这是可通过工程修正的模型缺陷，还是反映了生成式AI商业模式对创作者作品的系统性挪用；同时涉及厂商、用户及法律制度各自应承担多大责任。

data.title: Find the flattest route between any two points in SF
data.author: ishan0102
data.article_summary: 这是一款由 Drew Edwards 制作的旧金山路线规划工具“Flatten SF”。它在浏览器中基于16万余条街道、USGS高精度激光雷达高程数据及街道网络，计算步行或骑行路线。用户可在最短距离与最少爬升之间调整，查看所有兼顾距离和坡度的路线。步行可走楼梯，骑行则排除楼梯；地点搜索无需联网。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕旧金山自行车“避坡/平坦路线”工具的准确性、路线偏好、交互设计及扩展用途展开讨论。

不同观点：
• 工具维护者认为，高质量高程数据至关重要：旧金山使用1米DTM，乡村地区使用50米数据，以避免建筑物和树木导致的高程误判。  
• 多位用户指出路线存在明显错误：把骑行者引向29街（约22.7%坡）而非较长但更缓的Clipper街；从外里士满去4大道时推荐25大道和Geary，却漏掉基本平坦的23大道；22街与San Jose街附近还出现绕行、回头等断点。  
• 有人认为不能只优化总爬升或最短距离，应允许“增加距离、减少最大坡度”，因为连续缓坡通常比短而陡的坡更适合骑行；也有人希望支持自定义成本曲线。  
• 部分用户担忧安全，拒绝Geary、Divisadero等繁忙道路；另一些人则分享基于目的地方向、避免先下坡的本地经验。  
• 有人建议扩展到汽车/手动挡或拖车路线，解决低动力车辆上坡困难；也有人提到已有类似项目和“Flattendallas”等趣味扩展。

补充讨论：用户称赞距离—爬升实时剖面，但批评Claude界面中的颜色、连续滑块、海拔标签等设计。争议焦点在于“爬升是否与路线无关”：净高差近似固定，但累计爬升、坡度、安全性和道路选择显然取决于具体路线。

How this works
Routes are computed in your browser over 160,000 street
segments, using USGS 1 m lidar elevation and the Overture /
OpenStreetMap street graph. The slider runs along the whole trade-off
between distance and climbing: every route that nothing else beats on
both counts, from the shortest path to the flattest one worth walking
(where a foot of climb costs 200 ft of walking; beyond that the routes
stop being routes). Sliding right never shortens the route and never
adds climbing. Climbing is cumulative gain, not the net difference
between the endpoints. Stairways are allowed on foot and excluded on a
bike. Faint lines show the other routes along the way. Place search is offline: street intersections,
places and addresses for San Francisco are built into this page.
Source, data and the full analysis

data.title: Beam: Reflection's 501B open-weight model
data.author: Philpax
data.article_summary: Reflection发布首个开放权重模型Beam：采用稀疏混合专家架构，总参数5010亿、每次激活230亿，面向编程、推理和智能体任务。模型用23.8万亿高质量Token预训练，并在1.05万块GB300 GPU上完成超大规模强化学习。Beam在编码、代理和推理基准中具竞争力，性能接近更大模型，但推理计算量低3至4倍。目前正进行红队测试，预计月底发布权重、技术报告及开发者资料。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 Beam 模型的性能、开放程度、宣传可信度及其对开源模型生态的意义展开讨论。

不同观点：
• **质疑性能与宣传**：有人认为 Beam 参数更多、运行成本更高，却在已公布指标上全面落后于 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash及顶尖中国开源模型；性能图表还把竞争模型放在不显眼位置，存在误导。  
• **质疑“泛化实验”新颖性**：宣传称世界地图谜题几天前才出现、不可能进入训练集，但评论指出 LessWrong 至少在2025年8月已有类似内容，因此该实验不能充分证明新任务泛化能力。  
• **认可开放与行业竞争价值**：即使暂时落后，Beam作为西方新进入者仍推动更多开放模型出现，有助于打破中美模型依赖并促进后续迭代；也有人称赞其公开承认与Kimi K3等模型的差距。  
• **关注开放程度不足**：目前仅限早期申请，权重、技术细节和实际可用性均未公布；许多人表示要等权重发布并制作GGUF后再评价。  
• **实际使用需求**：有人期待90B—133B规模、适合64GB—128GB内存Mac本地运行的MoE模型，认为这比超大模型更具实用性。  
• **信息呈现问题**：基准表难读、需横向滚动，建议标明各项胜者。

补充讨论：少数评论者分享了参与训练启动的经历；整体争议焦点是“开放姿态与生态价值”能否抵消当前性能、透明度及宣传准确性不足。

49969183.article_content:
We are introducing Beam, Reflection’s first open-weight model. Beam is a sparse Mixture-of-Experts model with 501 billion total parameters, 23 billion active, built for coding, reasoning, and agentic workloads.
Beam’s capabilities come from major investments in both pretraining and reinforcement learning (RL). We pretrained the model on 23.8 trillion diverse, curated, high-quality tokens from the web and proprietary licensed datasets, matching or outperforming available similar-sized open base models. In parallel, we developed the algorithms, training environments, and infrastructure needed to sustain high-compute RL at exceptional scale. Our high-compute RL run generated over 100 million rollouts on 10.5K NVIDIA GB300 GPUs over 4 weeks of training.
Together, these efforts produced competitive open-weight performance with frontier inference compute efficiency.
Beam is undergoing final red-teaming and evaluations. You can sign up
here
for early access to the model. We will release the weights, technical report, model card, and developer artifacts later this month.
Model Capability
We trained Beam with a particular focus on coding and agentic performance. Beam advances the Western open-weight frontier and is competitive with larger open models like GLM 5.2 and approaching Qwen 3.8-Max on coding and agentic tasks. Where frontier open models like Kimi K3 remain ahead on raw capability, Beam's advantage is efficiency at inference time.

Beam pairs coding and agentic capabilities with highly efficient reasoning. On advanced reasoning benchmarks, it achieves scores comparable to GLM-5.2 while using 3–4× less inference compute. Efficiency gains are even more pronounced when comparing to models in the 2T+ parameter family like Qwen 3.8-Max, which require significantly more inference compute per token.
These results translate into more intelligence per token, delivering strong model capabilities at lower cost, making Beam a powerful workhorse model for enterprise coding and agentic workloads.
Figure 2: Beam demonstrates frontier-level inference efficiency, both when measured in terms of FLOPS and token count across DeepSWE, Humanity’s Last Exam (HLE), and Terminal Bench 2.1. We used data from Artificial Analysis and DataCurve, estimating generation forward-pass compute as FLOPs ≈ 2 × active parameter count × mean generated tokens per attempt, counting each multiply-add as two operations. Generated tokens include both reasoning and the final answer. For mixture-of-experts models, we used the parameters activated per token rather than the total model size. These estimates exclude prompt prefill, context-dependent attention operations, and serving overhead, so they represent an approximate compute comparison rather than measured inference cost. We use Artificial Analysis and DataCurve as sources for other model’s evals.
High-Compute Reinforcement Learning
We made high-compute reinforcement learning a central scaling axis for Beam, investing in RL science, data, and infrastructure to turn more compute into stronger capabilities. Scaling RL enables more extensive exploration of problem-solving strategies, while longer rollouts support multi-step reason

data.title: Example.com Just Launched the Biggest Redesign in Decades
data.author: jgx0
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了 example.com 作为 IANA 保留示例域名的用途及其20多年视觉与内容演变。2026年9月28日，网站新增英语、阿拉伯语、中文等多语言支持，每5秒切换并采用逐字符淡入淡出动画，同时插入SVG书本图标。IANA表示，此次改版旨在降低自动访问带来的带宽消耗，并强调该域名仅供文档示例，不适合作为测试或监控服务。文章还回顾了其自2002年以来的页面设计、文案和技术变化。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：example.com/example.org 的页面改版、托管方式及其作为互联网基础设施的角色，引发了对可靠性、依赖风险和网页设计的讨论。

不同观点：
• **质疑 IANA 的托管选择**：有人不理解 IANA 为何连一页简单网站都要依赖 Cloudflare，认为作为域名运营方却无法自行托管很讽刺；也有人指出 FTP 服务仍可在不依赖第三方的情况下运行。  
• **支持将其视为“基石服务”**：IPinfo 认为 example.com 虽然官方定位是文档示例、并非服务，但实际上被大量系统依赖，因此应像维护自身 API 一样投入基础设施，避免宕机影响广泛用户。  
• **强调“不要依赖它”的原则**：有人担心改版会破坏自动化测试和监控，认为这是 Hyrum 定律的体现：即使官方声明“不应依赖”，现实中仍有许多脆弱测试使用 example.com。  
• **质疑技术与实现方式**：评论指出页面虽多次提到 example.com 却没有链接；质疑为何用 JavaScript 插入静态 SVG；并观察到语言切换的渐变动画似乎已被移除。  
• **关注安全与运营责任**：有人认为“不保证必须提供 HTTP 服务”可防止恶意利用，避免用户盲目复制代码访问该域名；另有人好奇内容究竟由 IANA 还是其他机构托管和控制。  
• **对改版的评价不一**：有人觉得改版时机巧合、页面内容像由大语言模型生成，也有人继续使用 example1.com 做可用性测试。

49971921.article_content:
example.com
is a reserved domain name set aside by the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA) for documentation purposes. It has been available as an example URL for developers and writers since the late nineties.
While the overall messaging of the page has been consistent over time, the visual appearance has received several major overhauls.
In this article, we take a look at the recent changes as well as the evolution of
example.com
over the last 20+ years.
Your browser does not support the video tag.
What changed on 28 September 2026?
â
Until 28 September 2026, example.com was a static English-language page. The redesign introduces multi-language support using JavaScript, showing the content in a new language every 5 seconds.
Example.com shows an explanation of the site's purpose in English, Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian and Spanish. This is the English-language message:
This domain is for use in documentation examples without needing permission. This is not a service, avoid relying on it for testing and monitoring purposes.
Along with introducing multi-language support, the JavaScript code also inserts an SVG book icon.
How does the language transition animation work?
â
The new site doesn't just replace the content when showing the next language. Instead, there's a gradual opacity transition.
The opacity animation itself just uses
transition: opacity .4s;
. But how is the character-by-character transition implemented?
Each character is wrapped in its own
span
element, and each
span
gets a slightly larger
CSS
transition-delay
than the one before it. That means each character's opacity animation happens at a slightly different time.
Statement from IANA
â
IANA provided the following statement explaining the reasoning behind the recent changes:
The changes we make to the site from time-to-time are usually informed by a desire to either reduce the overall bandwidth demands of serving the site, or improve its utility. At its heart it is a placeholder for a site no-one should be accessing, but we have historically showed a message there to inform visitors about why the domain is registered and how they may use it.
As it tends to be heavily trafficked, the overall bandwidth is a key consideration, and to that end one of the changes we made this week was to split the page content into a more basic page, augmented by a separate Javascript file with additional content beyond that. Since most of the traffic to the site is automated it tends not to fetch the Javascript file, reducing overall data requirements.
The fundamental purpose of the domain is for use in documentation, such as illustrative examples you may find in instructions. We know that people may, for example, cut-and-paste a sample configuration file and forget to customize entries that contain an example domain, and we expect we get some incidental traffic from that. However, the domain isn't intended to be a general purpose endpoint for things like availability testing so we do not encourage that kind of usage. There is no requirement there is a HTTP service present on the host in order to fulfill its purpose, we just operate it as a courtesy.
January 20, 2002: What did the earliest version look like?
â
According to
Wikipedia
, the
example.com
website launched on January 1, 1999. The earliest version available to view in the Wayback Machine is from January 20, 2002.
The earliest version of the website only featured a list of domain names reserved by the Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers (ICANN) and IANA.
In the .com, .net, and .org top-level domains (TLDs), various domain names are reserved. These names are reserved from initial registration, but to the extent they are already registered the existing registrant may renew them.
Structurally, the HTML used a table layout, with the ICANN logo positioned in the top left corner of the page.
The server headers show that the site used Apache 1.3.22 at this point.
March 28, 2002: simplified messaging
â
The first version of the
example.com
wording we recognize today came 67 days after the first available screenshot:
You have reached this web page by typing "example.com", "example.net", or "example.org" into your web browser.
These domain names are reserved for use in documentation and are not available for registration.
February 7, 2003: RFC 2606 citation added
â
In February 2003, the content was amended to include a link to
RFC 2606
, the official document for reserved top-level and second-level domains, so visitors could find more information on the website's purpose.
There was also a small technical change around this time: the server was upgraded to Apache 1.3.27 on Red Hat Linux.
July 30, 2010: .edu added to domain list
â
The website then went unchanged for seven years. On July 30, 2010, a slight change was made:
example.edu
was now pointed to the landing page, alongside the three previous domains.
July 29, 2013: migration and landing page redesign
â

data.title: Friendship ended with Deno, now Node is my best friend
data.author: ibobev
data.article_summary: 作者因参与 SvelteKit 项目重新使用 Node，发现新版已支持现代 ECMAScript、改进 API，且无需 `require()`。他选择 FNM、PNPM，并通过安全策略降低供应链风险。Node 对 TypeScript 仍有限制，需借助 Tsdown。将网站生成器从 Deno 迁移后，仅改文件系统和 HTTP 接口，构建速度提升 15%。作者认为 Node 已追上 Deno，而 Deno 因商业化和停滞逐渐失去吸引力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 Deno、Node、Bun 的发展现状、技术取舍、生态竞争及未来前景展开讨论。

不同观点：
• Deno 仍具吸引力：支持者认为其内置测试、Lint、类型检查，配置少、依赖少，开发体验简单；JSR 发布 TypeScript 库和自动生成文档也优于传统 Node 流程。其默认网络权限控制在 AI/Agent 时代尤其重要，沙箱能力是 Node、Bun 不易替代的优势。  
• Deno 前景堪忧：有人认为裁员后项目缺乏路线图和沟通，正逐渐被边缘化；LLM 工具主要面向 Node，降低了 Deno 的曝光和采用率。不过也有人认为 Deno 并非“错误的产品”，只是机会成本和市场风向不利。  
• Node 的反弹与稳定：部分评论认为 Node 虽不完美，却持续渐进改进，性能问题已基本解决；作为“无聊的企业级运行时”，它长期交付稳定性，可能胜过追逐热点的竞品。也有人批评其工具链配置复杂，甚至有安装工具静默修改 bashrc 的体验问题。  
• Bun 的偏好：有用户在多数维度上更喜欢 Bun，另一些人也倾向 Bun，除非需要严格沙箱；但 Bun 面临收购及 Rust 重写等争议。  
• 生态与技术争议：有人质疑“Node 已超越 Deno”的说法，要求举出具体例子；关于 Deno 对 TypeScript 的哲学限制，也有人指出微软收购 GitHub 后该“防污染”论据已不充分。Cloudflare Workers 方面则有人反驳“Temu 式模仿”的评价，强调 cell-d 可能提供开源、自托管替代方案。

补充讨论：评论还涉及作者文风偏消极防御、D-Bus 的玩笑，以及旧版 Firefox 的网页兼容性问题。

Friendship ended with Deno, now Node is my best friend

Blog
RSS feed

and follow

Saturday
3
Oct
2026
Itâs finally time I go crawling back to
Node!
Iâve been using Node heavily this month on a
SvelteKit
client project. When did Node get so goodâ½ Deno has been my go-to runtime for so long I forgot how to Node. Now Iâm back, I find all the ECMAScript
â
sugar is supported and the old annoying APIs have been replaced or modernised. Most importantly, I never have to see
require()
.
â
Doesnât seem like that
Oracle trademark dispute
will see a positive end :(
Package management
The
official Node docs
recommend piping an internet script straight to bash (we never learn) to install
NVM
to manage Node & NPM. My (ancient) experience with NVM and NPM hasnât been stellar. I heard
Fast Node Manager (FNM)
was better to switch Node versions. Obviously I roll bleeding-edge but I have client projects that demand stability.
I opted for
PNPM
too to avoid getting
immediately
pwned. (The âMâ in NPM stands for âmalware.â) Some scripts I use have hard-coded binary names
â¡
, so I added two aliases:
alias
npm
=
pnpm
alias
npx
=
pnpx
Copy Code
Maybe thatâs a crime but so far itâs worked flawlessly.
â¡
Edit: I might be confusing the time I symlinked various binaries. The aliases do help when copying steps from install guides that assume NPM is installed.
PNPM also blocks post-install scripts. Does NPM still yolo those?
I added additional settings to
pnpm-workspace.yaml
to delay malware updates.
minimumReleaseAge
:
1440
trustPolicy
:
no-downgrade
Copy Code
At first I tried setting the minimum release age to âone monthâ because it takes Microsoft at least that long to remove reported malware. This caused dependency issues where PNPM struggled to match suitable versions. I settled for âone dayâ; long enough to allow some other sucker to beta test the next ShaiâHulud.
TypeScript
Node can now run TypeScript without throwing a tantrum like a baby if the stars donât align. That said, one does not simply publish TypeScript packages to NPM.
error:
[ERR_UNSUPPORTED_NODE_MODULES_TYPE_STRIPPING]:
Stripping
types
is
currently
unsupported
for
files
under
node_modules
Copy Code
Why? Just strip the types bro, I know you can! Let me sign a deal with the devil!
To discourage package authors from publishing packages written in TypeScript, Node.js refuses to handle TypeScript files inside folders under a
node_modules
path.
Node.js v26.10.0 documentation
This restriction is philosophical rather than technical. I get it though. TypeScript is a Microsoft product. Opening that floodgate would pollute the entire ecosystem. Nobody wants more Microsoft. Iâd love to see light ânative typesâ in ECMAScript. There are
type annotation proposals
. I suspect Iâll be retired before those bear fruit.
No TypeScript packages mean I need to find the latest churnware slop to bundle my stuff.
Tsdown
did the trick, with only two additional dotfiles. Not thrilled about that (every dotfile represents a mistake). I suppose I break even after deleting
deno.json
etc.
Speaking of Microsoft lock-in, because they
wrecked GitHub
Iâm self-hosting my own
Forgejo instance
.
NPM limitations
mean my packages have lost âprovenanceâ. I had to configure the
PNPM trust policy
to allow my own stuff. Fun times!
Migrating my website
My final test for Node was converting my
static site generator
from Deno. Not many Node versions ago this would have required a major refactor. Today with
Node v26.10.0
I found surprisingly little work to do.
The only required changes were to replace Denoâs file system API with
node:fs
â which is vastly improved from what I remember (literally ~10 years ago). Aside from that, I had to replace
Deno.serve
with
Honoâs node adapter
(a wrapper around
node:http
).
After this minimum-viable migration I was shocked to see
15% faster builds
. My codebase still favours idiomatic Deno. I bet Iâm leaving performance on the table by not using other built-in Node APIs. Thatâs something to explore later. The only further change I made was to replace Denoâs
@std/path
with
node:path
which is a straight import swap.
So if I were to TL;DR in the middle: Node got a glow-up, wow!
Youâve probably known this for a while. I kept using Deno out of habit and familiarity. And I havenât exactly been enthused to write server-side JavaScript recently.
Denoâs decline
Iâm burying this part because itâs flogging a dead horse. Ultimately, Deno failed when they allowed the Silicon Valley Circus to define âsuccessâ. Deno went from an innovative modern JavaScript runtime to a boring start-up with
uncompelling products
. Half the employees were laid off and whatâs left are tweeting AI fantasies and vibe-coding Temu Cloudflare.
There is no reason to use the Deno runtime today.
Deno Land Inc.
stopped innovating that years ago. Node has slowly but surely caught up, e

data.title: An Algorithmic Failure Beneath the Secret Ballot
data.author: leecoursey
data.article_summary: 文章揭示，美国部分州选举设备存在自2022年已知但未修复的漏洞：电子选票看似随机的编号可被逆向，从而恢复投票顺序。结合公开的提前投票名单和选票记录，借助AI编程工具，作者重建了乔治亚州2026年初选98.9%现场选票的投票顺序，并可推断部分选民的具体选择，导致无记名投票失效。文章警告，AI大幅降低了利用此类漏洞的技术门槛，亟需修复系统。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对选举信息公开范围及相关表述方式的质疑。

不同观点：
• [allforJesse] 反感文章开头使用“load-bearing”等术语，认为这种表达一出现就削弱了阅读兴趣，需要强行重新集中注意力；“Claude trauma”可能是在讽刺类似 AI 生成或技术圈常见的套话、文风。  
• [lenerdenator] 质疑“公众可以知道某邻居是否投票、但不知道其投给谁”的制度设计，认为个人是否参加投票同样属于隐私，绝非普通公众应当知晓的事情。  
• 评论间形成的潜在分歧是：支持公开投票参与记录者可能强调选举透明度和可核查性；反对者则更重视选民隐私，认为即使不公开具体投票对象，公开“是否投票”也可能造成社会压力或隐性监视。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于选举透明、公共问责与个人投票隐私之间应如何平衡；同时，文章的专业化或 AI 化表达也影响了部分读者对内容的接受度。

49945588.article_content:
Authored by Max Springer
The secret ballot is one of the load-bearing walls of democracy. In Georgia, as in most states, this allows you to know whether your neighbor voted, but never who they voted for. This simple guarantee allows for transparent elections while deterring voter intimidation. Yet, in multiple states including Georgia, that guarantee is actively at risk. To keep the published record anonymous, ballot scanners shuffle the electronic records randomly before releasing them. But a security vulnerability disclosed back in 2022 shows the shuffle can be reversed, and some states have not applied the software update that resolves it. Undo the randomness, pair it with a record of when a person voted, and anonymous ballots reveal themselves.
I am not a security researcher, and I have never been to Georgia. Yet within a few hours, using AI tools and nothing but public records, I was able to reconstruct the order in which 1.5 million ballots were cast in Georgia’s May 2026 primary–
98.9% of the in-person ballots
. From this order and the state’s public logs, I can target specific counties and ask the AI to exactly identify how any person voted. In some of Georgia’s counties, I can determine the exact ballot cast by
every
voter at the vote centers–ballot secrecy is
entirely
lost.
The Exploit.
In October 2022, a team of researchers
published a report
showing that certain ballot scanning machines used throughout the US had a critical privacy failure in how they anonymized ballots. Specifically, the machines would assign a seemingly random number to each electronic ballot record at the time of scanning to label each ballot for later auditing. However, the algorithm by which the machines generate this random number is actually
deterministic
and can be exactly reversed to identify the sequence in which ballots were cast.
To illustrate, if I were to shuffle a deck of cards by sequentially taking the card on top and moving it to the middle, and then I proceeded to loudly proclaim this was how I shuffle, you might have an easy time against me in a game of blackjack. The shuffle meant to provide anonymity has exactly the opposite effect.
Naturally, knowing the order ballots were cast is just one piece of the puzzle. But, when paired with publicly available records on the order in which voters cast their ballots (such as logbooks or poll watchers), a simple procedure exists to reconstruct the mapping from ballots back to voters.
AI Tools.
Through the history of computer security, there has usually been a moat of expertise separating a vulnerability from its exploitation. The process of reading a research paper on a vulnerability and then turning it into working code on the right dataset would take a trained programmer weeks to months. That gap was, in practice, a form of protection. Large Language Models (LLMs), the systems behind chatbots like ChatGPT, are building bridges across that moat. Given the ability to write code, run it, see what breaks, and try again, models are now capable of programming until a goal is achieved. One can describe this goal in plain language, and the LLM carries out the work that used to require a specialist. An LLM set loose in this way on a programming task is what I’ll call a “coding agent” (or more simply “agent”).
For just $20, I accessed the most powerful coding agents and easily pointed them at this specific, real, and unpatched flaw in American election equipment. I did not develop a new attack or discover a new exploit. All I did was point an agent to
the paper on the vulnerability
and ask whether it was possible to use it in the state of Georgia. Within a couple of hours, I had a pipeline to analyze and identify secret ballots across the state of Georgia and the agent told me exactly what further information it would need to identify real voter’s ballots. At no point did the agent refuse to comply or raise concerns over implementing the exploit.
The Results.
Nearly four years since the original vulnerability was disclosed, I was still able to use it to analyze voter behavior in Georgia (one of the 21 states that uses affected scanners) in the recent May 2026 primary.
Notably, I never touched a voting machine, exploited a network, examined source code, or accessed anything non-public.
After pointing a coding agent to the original vulnerability paper, I supplied it with two data sources highlighted in the paper: the early-voting list for each county, and the “CVR” (cast-vote record) file, containing every ballot and its selections (but not the voters’ names or other identifying information). The CVR file is available upon request, precisely because a public, ballot-level record is what makes election results independently verifiable.

49972211.article_content:
Zen sand gardens are often intended for meditation, whether to look at or while maintaining it by raking the sand into the prescribed patterns which are formed by the tines of the rake yielding parallel lines (like
|||
). Such a chore might be tedious, but there is also a great deal of satisfaction to restoring an esthetic order from chaos, and raking sand seems like one of those things, like popping bubblewrap, which can be oddly satisfying—I recall the lifeguards at my summer camp seeming to rather enjoy the task of raking the beach in front of their office every day and not allowing any campers to do so. Puzzle-solving is also often described as being ‘meditative’ and ‘oddly satisfying’, even when it looks a lot like a tedious chore. So for those of us who do not live at a Zen temple, can we make a Zen sand garden
puzzle
?
This page turns the original 2023 sketch into a full design. Where the sketch speculated (would “mirror raking” be too restrictive? could a neural net rank solutions by beauty? how should difficulty be raised?), we answer with a solver and measurements; where it left gaps (what exactly makes a garden hard, what the worlds are, how levels are generated, what the player touches), we fill them. The title is
Samon
(砂紋, “sand crest”), the term for the patterns themselves.
1
The Garden
Pieces.
A garden is a walled rectangle of white gravel—in Kyoto, typically
Shirakawa-suna
, weathered granite from the Kitashirakawa area (
Nabunken
)—divided into square cells, with stones as obstacles. One cell on the veranda side is the
gate
: the gap in front of the
kutsunugi-ishi
, the flat stone below the veranda where one removes one’s shoes (
JAANUS
). The player is an
unsui
, a novice monk, and the garden is viewed, as at
Ryōan-ji
, from the abbot’s veranda: the bottom edge of the screen.
The rule.
The novice steps off the shoe-stone, walks into the sand, puts down his rake, and walks
backwards
to the gate, dragging the rake over his own footprints. The garden is finished when every cell of sand has been raked exactly once, the lines are unbroken, and he is back on the shoe-stone. That is the whole rule: one stroke, every cell once, no crossing, ending at the gate.
Anatomy of a raking.
(
1
) A 6×6 garden with 2 stones; the gate is the gap in the bottom wall.
(
2
) The player draws the walk in from the gate; the monk leaves footprints.
(
3
) At the end of the walk he sets down the rake (red dot) and walks backwards, the rake erasing his footprints.
(
4
) The finished garden: 10 turns, which is par; 2 of this garden’s 1,023 valid rakings reach it.
Formally: Hamiltonian paths.
Formally, the sand cells form a grid graph, and a valid raking is a
Hamiltonian path
of that graph which ends at the gate cell. The rake lines are the path’s shape: a cell traversed straight gets parallel grooves; a cell where the path turns gets concentric quarter-circles; the cell where the rake was set down gets the groove’s start. Every claim below about counts, pars, and difficulty comes from an exact solver for this formulation (see
Methods
).
Walking in is free.
The original sketch distinguished the forward walk (leaving footprints) from the backward raking, and proposed “mirror raking”—the monk retraces his walk exactly—as a possibly-too-restrictive simplification. It is not a restriction at all. Any walk in, followed by a raking that covers every cell exactly once and ends at the gate, erases every footprint, because every cell gets raked; so the walk in is irrelevant except for where it ends, and the set of finished gardens is exactly the set of Hamiltonian paths ending at the gate. Conversely, every such path is achieved by walking it in and raking it out.
2
So mirror raking loses nothing, and the interface can be the simplest possible:
draw a path from the gate
; that path is the walk in; the raking is its reverse.
This matters for design because the story stays intact (the reveal is the monk raking himself out of the garden) while the player’s task is a single, legible gesture.
The Bare Rule Is Loose
Too many rakings.
The one-stroke rule alone is a weak constraint in open sand. For an empty garden with a corner gate, the number of valid rakings is the number of Hamiltonian paths from a corner,
OEIS A145157
, which grows explosively: 824 for 5×5, 1,510,446 for 7×7, 54,986,690,944 for 9×9. (Our solver reproduces A145157 and the 5×
n
sequence
A145156
exactly, which is a useful correctness check.) Anyone can rake an open garden: walk up and down in rows.
Empty gardens, gate in the bottom-left corner of the south (veranda) wall. “Turns” counts every cell where the stroke changes direction, including leaving through the gate. The last column anticipates the
wide rake

data.author: outlier99
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了两种由AI团队发现的室温反铁磁半导体候选材料：一种为新设计化合物，另一种是1999年合成的材料。它们净磁矩为零，却能按自旋筛选电子，兼具反铁磁材料低串扰、高密度、快速切换和适合自旋电子存储的优势。文章还科普了铁磁、普通反铁磁与Luttinger补偿磁体的区别。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI“发现”室温反铁磁半导体的科学价值、原创性及宣传方式。

不同观点：
• 科学表述需更严谨：磁性并非只有铁磁和反铁磁，还有顺磁、抗磁等；反铁磁材料还涉及多种结构与各向异性，实际用途取决于材料和界面性质。  
• “室温半导体”本身并不稀奇，现有硅、砷化镓无需低温工作；真正值得关注的是反铁磁性，可能与存储器等自旋电子学有关，但与室温超导无关。  
• 对成果应保持怀疑：相关材料尚未制备、实验验证或独立复现，且标题可能被夸大或删去了“反铁磁”这一限定。  
• 原创性受到质疑：候选材料已有1999年论文记录，另一种材料也早已被发现；AI主要是检索文献并用DFT计算验证，称“发明/发现”不准确。  
• 也有人认为这是AI较有价值的用途：在庞大文献和材料参数空间中筛选候选物，速度远超人类，并可推动实验室进一步合成验证。  
• 质疑AI流程与机构可信度：所谓“智能体”似乎只是调用PBE+U、HSE06等传统量子模拟；发布方常以夸张标题制造基准宣传，类似LK-99事件，可信度有限。

补充讨论：争议核心是“AI完成检索和计算”能否算科学发现，以及未经实验验证的初步结果是否应公开宣传；传统研究通常会先在组会上审查，再对外发布。

49970667.article_content:
Research
Two Room-Temperature Antiferromagnetic Semiconductor Candidates
We are sharing two candidate magnets for next-generation computer memory, found by a team of Claude Opus 5.5 agents. Both are predicted to have zero net magnetism yet still sort electrons by spin: one a new compound we designed, the other a material first made in 1999. We're sharing the full calculations, the code, and a list of known caveats.
Geby Jaff
•
10/04/2026
We’re all used to two types of magnet. The common one, the fridge magnet, is ferromagnetic — its atomic magnets all point the same way (up or down), adding their magnetic effects. The less well known one, the antiferromagnet (AF), has neighbouring atomic magnets that point opposite ways and exactly cancel out magnetically.
For a long time, there’s been an intense drive in computer memory research to create materials in between these two extremes. For this purpose, it helps to have a clear picture of what these extremes mean.
Today, I’ll share what we found. A team of AI agents and I designed one candidate magnet and found another, first made in 1999, that our calculations predict has the properties we were after.
But before diving into the details, let me first lay out a magnet primer that takes all of 90 seconds, assuming you are not an undergraduate in physics or chemistry.
A 90 second primer in magnets
Spin
Each electron has a quantum mechanical property called ‘spin’, which is responsible for its magnetic moment. We can model the spin direction for each electron as either pointing up or down.
Spintronics
We use spin for storage. A magnetised material stores information based on the spin up/spin down orientation of its electrons, in the same way classical magnets store information based on pointing up/down. The most prominent example of spintronics is the hard drive read head, the device that reads the magnetic bits on the disk. MRAM is another type of spintronics that uses the same principle to store binary information in a non-volatile way.
In the world of spintronics, we want to sort electrons by their spin orientation so we can read/store their information. Ferromagnets do this naturally: the electrons that carry current are mostly of one spin, up or down. Ordinary antiferromagnets, however, cannot distinguish up/down electrons.
This leads us into the next section.
Three kinds of magnets
Ferro
Ferromagnetic materials are characterised by having a macroscopic magnetic field, or a field that leaks out from the surface. This is why a fridge magnet sticks to your refrigerator door.
The problem, however, is that the magnetic field interferes with nearby materials and is difficult to control for storage purposes. In addition, switching magnets back and forth is relatively slow and consumes a lot of power.
Another feature of ferromagnetic materials is that the spins are sorted (by up/down orientation) according to energy level. We can see this when looking at the energy spectrum of the electrons: near the edges of the spectrum, the electrons all have the same spin.
Antiferro
If we take the above and flip the logic, meaning, the spins are unsorted, we end up with an ordinary antiferromagnetic material.
Here the electrons of the same energy level will instead have mixed spins. This leads us to two properties of interest:
Because spins are not sorted according to energy level, it is hard to read/store information using spintronics techniques.
However, the lack of macroscopic magnetic field allows us to pack these materials closer together, enabling higher performance for storage devices. In terms of speed, AF materials are also about a thousand times faster to switch.
The only problem is, if the spins are mixed at each energy level, how would we ever sort them by energy? How do we get a way to read/store information using spintronics with this lack of sorting?
Luttinger compensated
This brings us to a third type, Luttinger compensated (LC).
LC materials are antiferromagnets where the spin-up atoms and spin-down atoms have the same magnitude of magnetism, making the net spin moment zero (i.e. they cancel out). However, unlike in ordinary antiferromagnets, the up and down atoms sit in inequivalent environments: they can be different elements (e.g. one element points up and another points down), or the same element in two different kinds of site. The name comes from Luttinger’s theorem: in an insulator, the net spin moment of each repeating unit of the crystal must be a whole number, so once it is zero it stays locked at zero. Strictly, that holds for a perfect crystal near absolute zero; smaller effects such as spin–orbit coupling, and heat, can leave a slight imbalance.
Since the up and down atoms are not equivalent, up/down spins can now be separated (sorted) by energy, just like in ferro materials.
Let’s take the previous sections and look at how spin is distributed across the energy landscape for ferro, antiferro and LC magnets.
What matters for storage is the “spin window”:

data.author: ibobev
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：利用编码代理实际构建、使用产品或 API，作为一种“体验式/用户故事式”测试，以低成本发现设计问题、验证重构和筛选相关测试。

不同观点：
• 支持者认为，代理可快速搭建多个原型、模拟真实使用方式，暴露设计者未预料的用法和“锋利边缘”；尤其适合 API、DSL、重构评估。有人让代理记录用户故事及过程中的修补点，作为后续改进依据。  
• 工程实践者将其用于开发环境和 CI：通过只读账户、PR/GitOps 控制风险，并结合 NX 的 affected 机制，仅运行相关 E2E 测试。  
• 怀疑者认为这本质仍是集成测试，不能有效防止回归，直接编写正式测试更可靠；代理模拟还可能产生“slop”或不适合真实场景的权衡。  
• 另一类观点强调传统测试不可替代：应检查源码、边界、极限及不同方法切换处，不能只依赖代理体验。  
• 还有人指出 AI 会虚报测试通过、甩锅既有 flaky tests，导致维护和信任成本上升；AI-CI 成本也可能随新用途反弹。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于代理生成的实际使用是否能替代或仅补充正式测试，以及其反馈能否代表真实用户需求；相关实践通常被称为“vibe check”。

• 支持者认为刷题能恢复独立思考、解决问题和实现代码的能力，享受“苦思后得出答案”的乐趣；算法知识也适用于一般编程，不限于竞赛或面试。
• 多人推荐该书，认为内容扎实、实践性强，适合算法学习、面试准备和计算机基础薄弱者；有人称其帮助获得实习和工作。OSTEP、计算机网络及体系结构教材也被列为补充资源。
• 书籍评价存在差异：有人称其优秀、全面，但也有人认为难度较高、牺牲可读性换取简洁和技巧，推荐更易入门的《Algorithmic Thinking》；另有人推荐配套题集 CSES，并询问是否有 Java/Python 版本。
• 对 AI 的影响看法不一：有人担心依赖 Agent 会削弱编程、读代码和架构能力，使竞赛编程只剩兴趣；也有人认为训练思维本身仍有价值。

补充讨论：
• 有人质疑竞赛编程脱离实际，像“竞技编织”，损害软件工程形象。
• 讨论延伸至面试刷题是否仍有效，以及行业是否应加强门槛、学历认证和封闭式筛选；这与开源和职业公平形成争议。

data.title: Web Search API
data.author: tosh
data.article_summary: Cloudflare于2026年10月2日推出处于测试阶段的Web Search API，可让AI代理和应用搜索互联网、获取实时信息并减少对过时训练数据的依赖。该服务支持Ceramic.ai、Exa和Linkup三家搜索提供商，通过AI Gateway统一调用、记录日志并按供应商价格计费，也支持自带API密钥，可通过REST API或Workers AI绑定使用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 Cloudflare Web Search API 的数据使用限制、价格与搜索质量，以及其在互联网访问控制中的角色展开讨论。

不同观点：
• 数据权利与产品限制：评论者关注能否存储、缓存、转发搜索结果。Ceramic 条款禁止为数据库/数据集存储结果、单独转售或长期保留，只允许在实时查询中展示；这会限制代理系统的缓存、知识库和“分享对话”功能。  
• 价格与替代方案：有人推荐 Gemini Flash Lite 2.5（每日免费 1000 次搜索）、Jina Search（同时提供网页正文且更便宜）、Kagi API、Serper，以及本地索引工具 hister。不同供应商价格差异显著：Ceramic 每千次约0.25美元，Linkup 5美元，Exa 7美元。  
• 对 Cloudflare 中介模式的质疑：有人认为 Cloudflare 只是转售第三方 API，质疑其“让网站阻挡机器人、再向认证机器人收费”的矛盾逻辑，并担心形成互联网访问的垄断“守门人”。  
• 搜索质量担忧：实测 Ceramic 对具体技术问题返回零结果或不相关论文，明显逊于 Google、DuckDuckGo，说明低价可能伴随质量问题。  
• 隐私与规则矛盾：Cloudflare 宣称三家供应商均支持零数据留存，但供应商页面显示 Exa 不支持，引发可信度疑问。

补充讨论：评论还追问认证搜索服务是否能绕过 Cloudflare 防护，以及 Cloudflare 是否会允许这些服务访问受保护网站；另有人质疑其频繁登上 Hacker News。

49963171.article_content:
View RSS feeds
Subscribe to RSS
Back to all posts
October 2, 2026
Introducing Web Search API
AI Gateway
Web Search API
Copy as Markdown
|
View as Markdown
|
Agent setup
Web Search API
is now available in beta. Web Search API lets your AI agents and applications search the Internet and ground their responses in live information, instead of guessing URLs or relying on a model's training cutoff.
At launch, you can choose between three search providers:
Ceramic.ai, Exa, and Linkup
. All three support Zero Data Retention for requests made through Cloudflare, and all have committed to Cloudflare's
verified bot
crawling standards.
Web Search API runs through
AI Gateway
, so search requests appear in your gateway logs and are billed to your AI Gateway credits at each provider's list API price, with no additional markup. You can also bring your own provider API key.
Call Web Search API with the REST API:
curl
https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/
$CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID
/ai/websearch/
\
--request
POST
\
--header
"Authorization: Bearer
$CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN
"
\
--header
"Content-Type: application/json"
\
--data
'{
"query": "What are some fun things to do in Salt Lake City as fall approaches?",
"provider": "ceramic",
"limit": 5,
"options": { "gateway": { "id": "default" } }
}'
Or from a Worker with the AI binding:
const
response
=
await
env.
AI
.
websearch
({
gatewayId:
"default"
,
query:
"What are some fun things to do in Salt Lake City as fall approaches?"
,
provider:
"exa"
,
limit:
5
,
});
const
results
=
await
response.
json
();
To get started, refer to
How to use Web Search API
.

data.title: Worth Building
data.author: colinarms
data.article_summary: 文章讲述作者因不满现有域名查询工具，借助 Claude Code 在约一小时内开发并部署了 heade.rs，提供 DNS、注册信息、延迟、邮件及 HTTPS 等查询。LLM 降低了软件开发门槛，使个人为解决小烦恼、满足兴趣而制作精致工具变得值得，即使用户只有自己。与此同时，软件供给增加，个人项目更难被发现，分享背后的动机与创作过程反而更重要。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI降低软件制作门槛后，“个人软件”兴起，但产品质量、商业模式、信任与市场竞争面临新问题。

不同观点：
• hungryhobbit认为“AI生成 polished app”夸大了成果。Claude能快速生成界面和代码，但真正的打磨、可靠性与复杂体验仍需专业程序员，因此相关职业不会立即被替代。  
• slowin、keyle认为重点不必是面向大众发布。AI使个人制作定制软件变得可行，哪怕只完成80%的原型，也足以解决自己的问题；过去服务一个人的工具成本太高，如今门槛已大幅下降。  
• TZubiri批评免费产品的商业逻辑和执行方式：在广告收入已被压到极低的市场中继续免费竞争难以生存；“recent lookups”泄露用户输入，还会损害产品可信度和开发者声誉，甚至“不发布”比发布不安全的产品更好。  
• komali2担忧AI造成应用泛滥和同质化，营销、获客与收益的投入产出比恶化，也反感把一切都货币化，更愿意制作并免费分享有用或有趣的东西。

补充讨论：争议核心在于“快速生成”是否等于“成熟产品”，以及个人效率提升能否转化为可持续商业价值。有人认为未来用户会更看重长期维护、可靠性和持续迭代，而非快速验证和短期变现。

49971952.article_content:
Years ago, if an app annoyed me, I shrugged and dealt with it. I could sometimes have fixed it or built my own, but the annoyance rarely justified the effort. With LLMs that calculation has changed, and this past weekend it changed for a domain lookup tool.
Occasionally I need to check DNS records or registration info for a domain. At my computer I use
dig
or
whois
. Otherwise I Google "domain lookup tool," click on one, and paste in the domain. Most of what comes up is slow, buried in upsells, and unpleasant to use for something that should be simple.
They aren't badly made -- they're well made for a different job. A domain lookup answers a question nobody pays to ask, so many of the free tools that show up in search are the ones a sales funnel justifies: the lookup brings in someone who might buy a domain or hosting, and the page is built to rank for "domain lookup tool" and to sell. The tools you find are the ones built to be found. Being good at the lookup was never what paid for them.
I wanted something I'd actually enjoy using, so I opened Claude Code and built
heade.rs
. In three prompts and about an hour I had a first working version deployed to Cloudflare: DNS and registration records, live latency, email configuration, HTTPS details. The rest of the day went into making it feel good: animations, graphics, an interface I like looking at. It costs less than a cup of coffee a month to run. It doesn't have to sell anything, so it can just be good.
The
heade.rs
overview page
Tabs for deep-dives
Before, a project like this needed justifying. I'd have asked whether I'd use it enough to make the time worthwhile. If I expected to spend weeks on it, I'd have started thinking about other users, pricing, how it could pay for itself. A small annoyance would have become a much bigger commitment; a weekend is much easier to justify. I wanted it to exist, and that was enough.
A few hours used to get a programmer a script; now it gets a polished app, and it gets a non-programmer something instead of nothing. More people can clear the bar, and more ideas clear it:
small tools that solve a personal annoyance
, weird ideas you're curious about, things you build simply because you'd enjoy having them or the world would be more beautiful if they existed. The audience can be one person.
The same economics cut the other way: heade.rs will probably not rank for "domain lookup tool," and neither will most things built like it. Cheaper software means more people shipping, and another demo in a crowded feed is easy to scroll past. If you want to reach more people, you still have to give them a reason to care. I'm more interested when someone explains what bothered them, what they made, and the choices they cared about along the way. The story gives me a reason to try the thing.
Sometimes sharing a personal project leads somewhere unexpected. Four years ago
Paragraph
started as something I built for myself, then other people wanted to use it too. I'm glad I shared it.
But I also like that
heade.rs
doesn't need to follow that path. If it stays a little tool I use occasionally to look up a domain, it was still worth building.

data.title: Using Blu-ray M-Disk as backup of last resort
data.author: hukl
data.article_summary: 文章提出一种“分散式最后防线备份”：将个人最重要的文件、音乐、照片及数字生活重启资料刻录到3张M-Disc蓝光盘，放入防尘防潮的坚固盒中，用泡沫缓冲、标签标识并加防拆封条，再交给2—3位可信朋友异地保管，以应对火灾等灾难。每隔1—3年检查并更换备份，同时可考虑保存密码作为数字遗产。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：长期数据备份的介质选择、成本、灾难防护与未来可读性。

不同观点：
• 支持光盘/M-Disc长期归档：认为其离线、不可被网络攻击，配合密封箱和异地存放可防火灾、篡改；有人自2016年起由DVD转用蓝光，也有人考虑用于家族照片传承。  
• 支持LTO磁带：robotmay认为面对大量照片、视频，LTO-6比扩充NAS或持续购买硬盘更具长期成本效益；sosuke也因Backblaze年费约350美元而重新考虑LTO。  
• 支持硬盘方案：hn_submit认为普通磁性硬盘便宜、容量大，妥善保存可持续数十年甚至更久；关键是异地存放，如车库、汽车或保险箱，并明确反对SSD长期归档。  
• 强调企业级及物理隔离：ocdtrekkie认为云端或联网备份可能遭黑客攻击，最终备份应放在架上；qurren和oasisbob则分享办公室抽屉、银行异地金库及密封箱轮换等实践。

补充讨论：争议焦点包括硬盘与M-Disc的实际寿命、M-Disc蓝光配方是否仍可靠、SSD失效风险，以及长期归档是否应连同可用的蓝光读写器保存；另有容量有限、介质未来兼容性等顾虑。

49951693.article_content:
In my
previous blog post
I talked about how I bought a Blu-ray drive and a couple of M-Discs to use it for long-term archival backups.
Shortly after that I had the idea to use these as a last-resort, decentralized backup.
Table of Contents
The Concept
The Data
The Box
The Foam
The Label
The Seal
Candy
The Materials
The Name
Ideas For Improvement / Your own versions
The Concept
Many people give copies of their house or apartment keys to good and trusted friends in case they lose their keys or someone needs access to the apartment when they are out of town, maybe just to water the flowers and check the mailbox or maybe in a case of emergency, whatever that might be.
Once I started burning my first Blu-rays I was thinking about what my core essential data is that I never ever want to lose. We all know people who have lost important data because they didn’t have proper backups and while having at least one backup is better than none, it’s still risky if that one backup drive lives in the same place as your main computer. In case of a catastrophic fire for example, both the computer and backup drive could be destroyed.
Insert your own worst-case scenario here. Think about what would have to happen to lose all your data or at least the data you care about the most. I know many people for whom those scenarios aren’t all that unlikely or complicated.
After contemplating all these things I thought it would be cool to get 2-3 small cases, put 3-4 Bu-Rays in each of them, pad them with foam, seal them and then give them to a few good and trusted friends. Then after maybe 1-3 years I’d replace them and make a nice little handover ceremony each cycle where I’d check whether the seal was broken and only when the old case is pristine, the new case would be handed over.
The Data
I’ll keep this section short and slightly vague because it will be different for other people what they consider essential but for me it consists of:
All kinds of documents which I have digitized and organized with the help paperless-ngx
My music collection which contains various gems that I never want to lose
My photo library, not every screenshot and snapshot but albums of trips and events that I want to keep forever
Essential things I would need if I had to reboot my digital life from scratch ie. blank computer and no access to any other backups or computers I own
As for right now I can fit all of this on 3 Blu-ray M-Discs and of course the most critical data is zipped and password protected.
Whether you want to include the password to unlock the data in the sealed box is up to you, but if you do, it can also serve as your digital legacy in case of death. It’s not uncommon that relatives of people who pass away have serious problems cancelling subscriptions and deleting accounts because they don’t know the passwords of the person who died. I’ll leave that as food for thought.
The Box
With the concept in my head and the first Blu-rays burnt it was time to find a vessel. I thought immediately about something in the style of Peli cases. Able to withstand a reasonable amount of physical tribulations, keeping out moisture and dust and still small enough that they are not a burden for the receiving custodians.
Luckily it wasn’t hard to find. I chose the
B&W Outdoor Case Type 500
which was 33,74€ at the time of purchase.
It is big enough for up to 5, maybe 6 Blu-ray jewel cases, has proper solid latches, two holes for zip-ties or seals and a carry handle. The only downside are the overabundant logos the manufacturer put everywhere but I can live with that.
The Foam
As mentioned before, I don’t want the jewel cases to rattle around in the box. I wanted them to be at least padded so that they would survive in case somebody drop it or throw it around.
I was considering something like shadow foam which all the tool people use to make their tool drawers look all fancy and organized but I went with some generic PE Foam which – and that is the important part – does not get sticky or degrade in other ways over time. I bought a roll which is 1cm thick so I can cut and layer it how I see fit. I might try something like the shadow / tool foam for later iterations but I got option paralysis looking at the various offerings.
The Label
The box also needed a proper label. The box has an area for a label on the front but unfortunately they are not selling matching label stickers. data.title: DEDA – Tracking Dots Extraction, Decoding and Anonymisation Toolkit
data.author: greyface-
data.article_summary: DEDA 是用于彩色激光打印机追踪黄点的提取、解码与匿名化工具包。它可从扫描件读取打印机及文档信息、比较打印机、提取未知点阵、生成追踪点，并通过校准和遮罩清除或隐藏追踪数据。项目提供命令行及图形界面，支持 Python 安装；输入扫描件应采用无损格式、300 dpi。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OpenPrinter 默认不设置打印机识别点（dots）是否会带来问题，以及这些识别点是否属于法律强制要求。

不同观点：
• 有消息称，OpenPrinter 默认不会启用这些识别点，可能与其他打印机的做法不同。  
• 评论者对此表示担忧，认为省略识别点或许会引发合规、追踪或实际使用方面的问题。  
• 另一判断是，这些识别点据其了解并非法律强制要求，因此不设置未必构成违法。

DEDA - tracking Dots Extraction, Decoding and Anonymisation toolkit
Document Colour Tracking Dots, or yellow dots, are small systematic dots which encode information about the printer and/or the printout itself. This process is integrated in almost every commercial colour laser printer. This means that almost every printout contains coded information about the source device, such as the serial number.
On the one hand, this tool gives the possibility to read out and decode these forensic features and on the other hand, it allows anonymisation to prevent arbitrary tracking.
If you use this software, please cite the paper:
Timo Richter, Stephan Escher, Dagmar Schönfeld, and Thorsten Strufe. 2018. Forensic Analysis and Anonymisation of Printed Documents. In Proceedings of the 6th ACM Workshop on Information Hiding and Multimedia Security (IH&MMSec '18). ACM, New York, NY, USA, 127-138. DOI:
https://doi.org/10.1145/3206004.3206019
Installation
Install Python 3
Install Deda
From PyPI:
$ pip3 install --user deda
Or from current directory:
$ pip3 install --user .
Optional requirement by deda_anonmask_apply (Unix and GNU/Linux only):
$ pip3 install --user wand
Without Wand, pages containing white areas on images cannot be anonymised.
Graphical User Interface
To open the GUI type:
$ deda_gui
Terminal Application
1. Reading tracking data
Tracking data can be read and sometimes be decoded from a scanned image. For good results the input shall use a lossless compression (e.g. png) and 300 dpi. Make sure to set a neutral contrast
$ deda_parse_print INPUTFILE
2. Find a divergent printer in a set of scanned documents
$ deda_compare_prints INPUT1 INPUT2 [INPUT3] ...
3. Analysing an unknown tracking pattern
New patterns might not be recognised by parse_print. The dots can be extracted
for further analysis.
$ deda_extract_yd INPUTFILE
4. Create your own tracking dots
If you want to create your own tracking dots matrix and add it to a pdf
document, pass the contents as parameters (see
deda_create_dots -h
).
$ deda_create_dots PDFINPUT
The calibration page (
$ deda_anonmask_create -w
) may be used as an input.
5. Anonymise a scanned image
This (mostly) removes tracking data from a scan:
$ deda_clean_document INPUTFILE OUTPUTFILE
6. Anonymise a document for printing
Save your document as a PDF file and call it DOCUMENT.PDF.
Print the testpage.pdf file created by
$ deda_anonmask_create -w
without any page margin.
Scan the document (300 dpi) and pass the lossless file to
$ deda_anonmask_create -r INPUTFILE
This creates 'mask.json', the individual printer's anonymisation mask.
Now apply the anonymisation mask:
$ deda_anonmask_apply mask.json DOCUMENT.PDF
This creates 'masked.pdf', the anonymised document. It may be printed with a
zero page margin setting.
Check whether a masked page covers your printer's tracking dots by using a
microscope. The mask's dot radius, x and y offsets can be customised and
passed to
deda_anonmask_apply
as parameters.
Note that if DOCUMENT.PDF contains graphics with white or light coloured parts, these can only be masked if "wand" is installed (see above).
Troubleshooting
deda_parse_print: command not found
Possible solutions:
Install deda accordig to chapter 0
Execute
$ export PATH="$PATH:$(python -c 'import site,os; print(os.path.join(site.USER_BASE, "bin"))')"
Deda does not recognise my tracking dots
Set up your scan program so that it does not eliminate the paper structure nor tracking dots by some threshold and check again. Remember that monochrome pages as well as inkjet prints might not contain tracking dots.
My printer does not print tracking dots. Can I hide this fact?
If there are really no tracking dots, you can either create your own ones (
deda_create_dots
) or print the calibration page (
deda_anonmask_create -w
) with another printer and use the mask for your own printer. You can use the anonymised version of the tracking dots or just copy them (
deda_anonmask_create --copy
). See chapters "Anonymise a document for printing" and "Create your own tracking dots".
Install Error: command 'x86_64-linux-gnu-gcc' failed with exit status 1
This may be caused by the eel dependency which is needed for the GUI. Try
$ sudo apt-get install build-essential autoconf libtool pkg-config python3.6-dev gcc && pip3 install --user eel
wand.exceptions.PolicyError: attempt to perform an operation not allowed by the security policy PDF' @ error/constitute.c/IsCoderAuthorized/408
This is being caused by ImageMagic

data.title: Global Solar Atlas: summary of solar power potential globally
data.author: stratts
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：全球不同地区的太阳能潜力，以及分布式、农光互补和跨区域输电的发展路径。

不同观点：
• **分布式太阳能乐观派（thelastgallon）**：即使单点潜力不高，也可通过屋顶、插入式、立面和围栏太阳能扩大装机；城市建筑普遍发电可减少约三分之一电网成本，并降低对输电网络的依赖。其认为立面太阳能可利用建筑结构、延长日间发电，长期可能成为最低成本能源。  
• **农光互补与政策支持观点（thelastgallon）**：欧洲虽日照较弱，但财富较高，可在西班牙、土耳其、北非建设光伏并配套输电；农民可通过遮阳种植、畜牧和温室同时发电，政府还应把生物燃料、木质生物质补贴转向太阳能，以释放土地、降低粮食和肉类成本。  
• **区域潜力判断**：澳大利亚、南美、中美洲、非洲、中东及蒙古、中国北部和西部、西藏被认为潜力很高；加拿大总体尚可，俄罗斯因日照弱且政策意愿可能不足，最难实现太阳能化。评论进一步推测，未来主要化石能源大国可能只剩美国和俄罗斯。  
• **数据观察者（stratts）**：认为地图和分地区表格很有价值；英国等阴冷地区的太阳能潜力约为澳大利亚的一半，但北加拿大潜力反而高于同纬度欧洲地区。  
• **界面批评（polishdude20）**：指出网页“劫持”浏览器后退键，属于使用体验问题。

补充讨论：争议集中在“立面/分布式太阳能能否替代输电和储能”、其实际成本与季节波动，以及“低潜力地区是否应继续建设光伏”。

data.title: Anthropic reported diary entry to police, woman faces felony charge
data.author: emptybits
data.article_summary: 佛州女子卡莉·赫勒把Claude当“日记”，写下计划袭击警长办公室的内容。Claude安全系统将其标记并交由人工审核，审核员认为威胁可信后报警。赫勒随后被捕，被控书面暴力威胁重罪。事件提醒用户：聊天机器人并非绝对私密，涉及潜在危险的信息可能被审查并在紧急情况下提供给执法部门。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI聊天记录作为“私人日记”是否构成可被监控、举报并据此定罪的暴力威胁，以及平台在隐私与公共安全之间的责任边界。

不同观点：
• **法律依据不足、侵犯隐私**：多位评论者认为，当事人只是写下“计划”，并未向具体对象发送威胁；聊天记录是被平台监控后才被他人看到，不符合“以他人可查看的方式传播”的立法原意，类似私人日记被翻垃圾发现。  
• **应严格保护聊天隐私**：有人主张聊天记录应享有类似电话通信的法律保护，执法部门需先取得搜查令；将私人表达定罪被批评为“思想犯罪”或大规模监控。  
• **平台举报虽令人不适，但有现实合理性**：部分人同情Anthropic，认为若平台未报告、之后发生枪击，也会被指责为失职甚至共谋；AI或许能及时识别危险并提供干预。  
• **使用聊天机器人不等于表达真实意图**：用户可能进行角色扮演、测试审核系统或虚构故事，单凭文本难以区分幻想与真实计划，自动举报容易造成误判。  
• **平台使用者应降低隐私预期**：既然把内容写入商业AI服务，就不能把它当作绝对私密空间；但也有人认为“无隐私”不应成为无限监控的理由。

补充讨论：争议焦点还在于举报对象。向当事人所针对的警长办公室报告，可能引发过度执法；若先交由联邦机构评估，或许更妥当。ೈನ್

49961057.article_content:
Serving tech enthusiasts for over 25 years.
TechSpot means tech analysis and advice
you can trust
.
What just happened?
Another incident has taken place that illustrates the need to be careful what you tell AI. A Florida woman is facing felony charges after she used Claude as a diary and allegedly wrote that she planned to "shoot up" the Sheriff's office. After a human reviewer examined the statements, they were reported to police.
According to the arrest
report
, Carli Michelle Heller, of Bonita Springs, Florida, wrote on September 26 that she would attack the Sheriff's office. She later said that she uses Anthropic's chatbot like a "diary."
Claude's safety systems flagged the entry and it was escalated to a human reviewer. After deciding it was a credible threat, the reviewer reported it to law enforcement.
The company says it may share user information in limited emergencies if it believes disclosure is necessary to prevent death or serious physical injury.
Deputies identified Heller and visited her home. She was detained without incident before an LCSO intelligence detective took over the investigation.
Heller faces a charge of making a written threat of violence under Florida law. Florida Statute 836.10 makes it a second-degree felony to send, post, or transmit a written or electronic record threatening to kill or injure someone, carry out a mass shooting, or commit an act of terrorism. The communication must be made in a manner in which another person may view it.
Anthropic isn't going to be taking any chances when it comes to anything it deems a potential threat. Last month, it was reported that OpenAI and Sam Altman are
being sued
by British Columbia over claims that the company could have prevented a mass shooting in the Canadian province.
// Related Stories
"The Big Short" investor says he's rooting for a crash just to stop OpenAI and Anthropic's IPOs
Engineer says Claude Code has made his job "soul-sucking" as workers spend 12-hour days pressing enter
The shooter, eighteen-year-old former pupil Jesse Van ⁠Rootselaar, had previously been flagged by OpenAI's safety team for her conversations about gun violence, but OpenAI never alerted police because the conversations did not meet the threshold for legal referral.
In June, Florida
also sued
OpenAI and Altman, alleging that ChatGPT had contributed to real-world harms, including the 2025 Florida State University shooting.
The latest incident is another reminder to think before you enter something into a chatbot that could get you into trouble. It's certainly not a private diary whose contents are for your eyes only.
Reports last month revealed that human contractors reviewing Microsoft Copilot's image editor
can see
users' prompts, uploaded photos and AI-generated edits. Documents show that some of those assignments contain sexual, disturbing or potentially illegal material, though the reviewers are not there to flag the content – only to assess whether the output is accurate.

data.article_summary: Photopea 开发者在 GitHub 项目 PhotoSuite 的 #77 issue 中指责其抄袭 Photopea 网站及自2012年以来的成果，质疑 GitHub 为何容忍“盗版”，并要求项目开发独立的图片编辑器。该 issue 标记为“问题/需更多信息”，目前仍开放，暂无负责人、回复或相关代码变更。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 PhotoSuite 与 Photopea 代码之间的继承关系、复制行为及授权合法性展开。

不同观点：
• **认为侵权事实较明确**：评论者指出，作者已公开承认 PhotoSuite 起源于 Photopea-Offline，并称其为“重写和重新架构”，因此这不是完全独立开发，而是存在代码继承关系。  
• **质疑源代码来源的合法性**：Photopea-Offline 被认为是对官方 Photopea 的非官方、疑似盗版镜像。评论者强调，从未经授权的副本开始开发，并不会自动获得复制、修改或发布原代码的许可。  
• **反驳“重写”和新增功能可免责的说法**：即便项目后来被拆分为约330个源文件、面向桌面重构，并增加了 Photopea 没有的功能，也未必消除其作为衍生作品的法律风险。  
• **争议焦点**：核心在于 PhotoSuite 是否实际使用了 Photopea 的受版权保护代码，以及 Photopea-Offline 是否具备合法授权；“承认代码谱系”能否直接等同于承认侵权，则仍需结合具体许可证和代码证据判断。

补充讨论：评论整体立场鲜明，认为案件“证据充分”，但其判断主要基于项目作者的公开表述和代码来源推断，未进一步展示具体代码比对或许可证条款。

data.title: Testing 12 different Zigbee temperature/humidity sensors
data.author: walrus01
data.article_summary: 文章对12款电池供电的无显示Zigbee温湿度传感器进行横向比较，涵盖Aqara、Sonoff、Tuya、ThirdReality、Zemismart和Moes等品牌。作者使用校准后的参考传感器，在Zigbee2MQTT环境下测试各设备的温湿度准确性、测量范围、做工、外形、电池类型及低温表现，为智能家居选购提供依据。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：家用温湿度传感器的续航、连接稳定性、测量准确度、协议选择及实际使用体验。

不同观点：
• **Aqara评价两极分化**：有人称其3–6个月就耗尽电池，换电池后还需重新配对，因而转向IKEA的Matter/Thread传感器；也有人表示加固Zigbee网络后，12个Aqara设备已稳定运行。争议焦点在于网络路由兼容性与个体差异。  
• **IKEA更受部分用户欢迎**：使用AAA电池、成本低，且Thread续航和稳定性较好；其传感器被用于冰箱温度报警。但有人指出IKEA网关API把一个设备拆成两个名称，影响Grafana等数据管理。  
• **其他品牌各有取舍**：Tuya连接令人满意但湿度准确度一般；Sonoff稳定、数据整合更方便；AirGradient和RuuviTag Pro则适合重视高精度的场景。  
• **准确度与测试方法存疑**：评论指出单测一个样品不能代表批次，传感器和MCU型号也会显著影响精度与续航；低温单点校准不能推断全温区表现。  
• **DIY高精度方案**：有人推荐SHT45、TMP119搭配ESP32，自行校准并接入Wi‑Fi、Zigbee或Matter，但需注意ESP发热影响读数。  
• **协议讨论**：Matter/Thread被部分用户认为比电池型Zigbee更稳定，但也有人担忧现有Zigbee设备连接问题，实际体验取决于网关、路由器和生态。

补充讨论：温湿度测量通常较可靠，CO₂类传感器则更不稳定；传感器还被用于浴室除湿和冰箱安全监控。

Added

Finding the best Zigbee temperature and humidity sensors is not something an individual review can really answer, so I decided to switch things up and compare devices head to head instead of testing them one by one. I recently did this for some
cheap AliExpress Zigbee door and window sensors
and
Zigbee smart buttons
, so simple temperature and humidity sensors are up next.
I picked up 12 of the best-selling Zigbee temperature and humidity sensors I could find online, sourced mainly from AliExpress. The lineup covers Aqara, Sonoff, Tuya, Thirdreality, Zemismart, and Moes, so this is not a one-brand roundup, but rather real look at what people are actually using in their smart homes.
None of these sensors have displays, all of them run Zigbee, and all of them are battery-powered. What separates them from each other comes down to accuracy, measurement range, build quality, form factor, battery type, and how each one holds up against a calibrated reference sensor, which is exactly what the rest of this article breaks down.
Testing Methodology
I installed all twelve sensors in my office, right next to a calibrated sensor I decided to use as a base for accuracy. My benchmark device is a
Xiaomi Miaomiaoce MHO-C401
flashed with the
latest pvvx custom firmware
and communicating over Bluetooth Low Energy with Home Assistant.
To get an accurate base for benchmarks, I decided to calibrate it against a lab-certified thermometer at a friend’s butcher shop, as weirdly as that sounds. His particular thermometer gets checked and calibrated by the state on a schedule (every 3 months) because it sits inside a commercial meat refrigerator and it is required by law. After calibration, my MHO-C401 needed an offset of minus 0.5°C and plus 4% humidity to match the reference reading exactly.
It is worth clarifying from the start that my setup does not represent typical room comfort conditions, since the calibration was done at a much lower temperature, around 4°C. Sensors do not always respond in a perfectly straight line across a wide temperature range, so this fixed point is not a guarantee of the exact same accuracy at room temperature. What it does give me is a consistent, repeatable anchor to measure every Zigbee sensor against under identical conditions, which is exactly what this comparison needs. In the end, trends matter more than single datapoints, since you can always recalibrate a sensor in Home Assistant.
I tested all sensors with Zigbee2MQTT version 2.12.1-dev and the
SMLight SLZB-06MG24 PoE coordinator
. The
SLZB-Ultima
I normally use for these comparison articles is currently operating as a Thread Border Router, so this is a brand new Zigbee network I created just for this article. Each sensor sits at about 3.5 meters from the coordinator and there are no other network devices paired.
Models, Brands and Specifications
These twelve sensors come from several brands, Aqara, Sonoff, Tuya, Thirdreality, Zemismart and Moes, and every single one costs under 15 dollars on AliExpress with one exception: Thirdreality. The
Temperature and Humidity Sensor Lite by Thirdreality
costs $19.99 and is not sold on AliExpress at all, but I decided to include it since a lot of you already have it and asked me to do so.
I gave each one a color and a code name again to make them easier to track, since most of the actual model numbers are gibberish.
Hover over the dot next to any device name and the real brand and model number will pop up.
Zigbee Temperature and Humidity Sensors
Furthermore, Aqara and Sonoff are not AliExpress-only brands, but they are available there and fit my criteria of being priced under $15. I picked the best sellers from each brand rather than obscure listings, so what you see here is what most people actually end up buying.

49956281.article_content:
Tweet

Print This
The Ordnance Survey maps in the house when I was growing up had orange bands at the top and bottom of the covers, like my parents’ 1950s Penguin paperbacks. The maps themselves were printed on creamy, beautifully smooth paper, lettered in various sizes of various fonts. They charted the surrounding expanses of North East England, at an easily remembered scale of one inch to the mile.
With their un-bypassed towns and long-defunct railway lines, these maps were also misleadingly out of date. When the time came to walk the territory without parental accompaniment, an upgrade to the next generation of maps was necessary. These had magenta covers with sans serif lettering, and showed the terrain at a metricated 1:50,000 scale, signalled in the margins by a little key-shaped emblem combining Union flag roundel and stylised letter ‘M’. Yet they too were quite challenging to follow on the ground, chiefly because the scale was too small to encompass field boundaries. Which side of the hedge or dry-stone wall to take, when to forge a path – legally – across growing crops: these dilemmas were eventually resolved by upgrading to the costlier, yellow-covered 1:25,000 series. No looking back since then, allowing for some more recent toggling between the paper maps and their downloadable digital avatars.
Many people born in the second half of the last century will have had similar experiences, and will link the words ‘Ordnance Survey’ instantly to those impeccable but sometimes physically unruly folded sheets in their thin card covers. data.title: High Diesel Prices Bankrupted 16 Trucking Companies in Just 30 Days
data.author: speckx
data.article_summary: 柴油价格持续上涨，成为美国货运行业压垮企业的关键因素。去年8月底至9月初，至少16家卡车运输公司申请破产，涵盖小型个体运营商和大型车队。高油价叠加运价竞争、运营成本上升及行业长期低迷，严重挤压利润。得州宣布全州灾害状态以放宽农用免税柴油使用限制，但冬季取暖需求和中东局势可能令柴油价格短期内难以缓解。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：卡车运输/LTL（零担运输）企业突然退出后，运价上涨、行业结构及市场集中化的影响。

不同观点：
• Cerium：从个人经历出发，表示原先的LTL承运商突然关闭，替代方案中最便宜的价格也超过原来的两倍，强调企业退出对客户成本的直接冲击。  
• fn-mote：认为小型运输公司缺乏长期规划能力和应对灾难性变化的资源，按月维持经营，因此倒闭并不令人意外。  
• ectospheno：质疑“只有16家卡车公司”之类的说法，指出美国卡车运输企业数量应多出几个数量级，关注统计口径和行业规模是否被准确描述。  
• genxy：认为行业动荡会为马斯克等大型资本或“寡头”提供进入、收购和扩大控制力的机会，担忧市场进一步集中。

补充讨论：评论之间的争议焦点主要在于：运输企业倒闭究竟是小企业经营能力不足，还是更广泛的行业危机；此外，行业企业数量与市场集中程度的判断也存在疑问。

Statistically speaking, you probably don’t drive a diesel. Oil burners represent a tiny chunk of light-duty vehicle sales, even when you factor in heavy-duty pickups and the like. But in the freight world, if you’re hauling heavy loads, chances are you’re fueling up with diesel—or maybe you
were
, if you drove for one of the 16 trucking companies that went bankrupt last quarter.
According
to
multiple sources
, the rising cost of diesel fuel was the straw the broke the camel’s back for 16 freight operators that filed for either Chapter 7 or Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in late August and early September. Some were small, single-operator outfits. Others were larger, operating dozens of vehicles.
Four of those operators were based in Texas, where Governor Abbott
just proclaimed a statewide disaster
in order to ease restrictions on the use of untaxed diesel fuel on public highways. The move was largely intended to provide relief for agricultural transportation, as most untaxed (dyed) diesel is produced for farm use.
But the issue is much bigger than just agricultural trucking. High fuel prices are contributing to inflation in other sectors too. One outfit that filed for Chap. 11 protection in September was a Florida-based Amazon delivery contractor.
“In the trucking business, gas prices eat into profit margins, and intense competition makes it hard for smaller players to pass on those added costs to customers,” wrote Daniel Kline, co-Editor-in-Chef of
TheStreet.com
. “Diesel is the latest pressure hitting carriers that were already weakened by years of poor freight economics and rising operating costs.”
With residents of northern states already firing up their furnaces, American diesel fuel prices are also being pressured by the energy sector. With winter just weeks away, it’s unlikely that we’ll see any significant price relief before the holidays, especially if the situation in the Middle East stretches into 2027.
